approach.method_basis: The Parent samples local molecular graph edits from one scored current state, normalizes identities, rejects duplicates and sends the first full tabu-admissible batch for evaluation. It then walks to the best accepted neighbor, including worsening moves, while retaining an independent best archive. Bond changes alter bond order; deletions remove atoms or leaves. Neither directly relocates an intact side group along an aromatic ring. The Parent already includes the repaired identity join and its established inverse-motif memory.
approach.novelty: Add one intact-substituent relocation along an existing aromatic ring edge. Detach an acyclic pendant group from an aromatic carbon and reconnect the same group to an adjacent aromatic carbon bearing a hydrogen. This changes substitution position while retaining the whole group, the ring framework and molecular formula. The move becomes an extra choice when the existing bond-change operator selects that attachment bond. Earlier branch deletion discarded groups; nitrogen exchange moved ring elements. This experiment instead reconnects an existing side group and incorporates neither earlier extension.

hypothesis: Extend the existing change_bond neighborhood with relocation of an intact single-attachment acyclic branch from an aromatic carbon to its adjacent hydrogen-bearing aromatic carbon, directly exposing substitution-position isomers while preserving the branch, ring framework and molecular formula.

finding_summary.headline: Ten intact-group position changes were evaluated, but none carried the improved panel score
finding_summary.insights: Direct positional accessibility is established: none of the ten scored products is reachable by a single original bond-order change, and each changes local motifs and measured score. Intact-group retention therefore avoids the necessary atom loss of branch deletion, but it does not reliably make a stronger neighbor. All four evaluated larger-branch relocations lose to their sources, including the methoxy and carboxyl shifts. The distinction between a successful panel and useful new molecules matters here: since no relocation is selected, the panel gain cannot be credited to descendants carrying a moved group. The expanded menu also changes proposal choices and batch competition among the original operators. The evidence supports a working positional channel and one local thiol-position gain, while leaving a reproducible score benefit from retaining a new position unresolved. The stronger sulfur-free aryl-amine series identified by the molecular assessment is an original-operator outcome and still contains strained nitrogen rings; other populations retain unusual sulfur and reactive heteroatom bonds. Conserving the existing group and ring has not established better stability or synthetic accessibility.

The three-seed macro mean nevertheless rose from 0.520918 to 0.525257, a paired gain of 0.004339 that exceeds the 0.002 target. One seed improved and two declined; the largest endpoint gain was in one DRD2 seed, while median_2 and sitagliptin endpoints were unchanged throughout.

molecular.headline: Sulfur-rich cages persist; a stronger aryl-amine family removes sulfur but retains strained nitrogen rings
molecular.overall_character: All supplied current and parent trajectories were inspected. Every objective has 900 entries, including 870 optimizer proposals, and none lacks trajectories. These are consistently substantial ring-containing molecules: ring-closure and branch presence rates are 1.0 throughout. Aromatic-token presence is also 1.0 on several populations, 0.9345 on the arylamide population, and 0.7184 on the sulfur-cage population. These are molecule-level text counters, not aromatic atom fractions, ring feasibility, or molecular conformations. The outputs range from recognizable indole carboxamides and aryl cyclic amines to heavily bridged N/O frameworks, long sulfur/oxygen side chains, and multiply bonded sulfur cages. Mean SMILES lengths range from 46.9 to 69.0; the main problem is not a population of trivial fragments or universally giant repeated assemblies. Rather, much of the visible variety changes decoration or connectivity within seed-specific complex families. Explicit charge and tetrahedral stereolabel rates are zero, despite potentially basic amines and stereogenic carbon or sulfur connectivity. Some current chemistry differs meaningfully from the parent, especially the sulfur-free aryl-amine leader, while other leading structures and entire chemical trajectories are unchanged. Apparent synthetic plausibility remains questionable and overall drug likeness weak because useful recognizable groups coexist with strained rings, unusual sulfur valence, reactive heteroatom-halogen bonds, and undefined stereochemistry.

per_task.generated_character: The compact leaders carry aromatic rings and amide or ketone carbonyls, but they separate into chemically different families. The best combines an alkyl-substituted unsaturated sulfur/nitrogen ring system, a primary carboxamide, and an acylated nitrogen bridging adjacent benzene carbons. That last unit is a strained benzene-fused small nitrogen ring, not an ordinary anilide. Related leaders retain the same constrained amide nitrogen with benzothiophene, aminomethoxy, or chloromethyl substitution. A more conventional ethoxy/methyl/thiol-substituted indole carboxanilide is also near the top. The final seed instead favors pyridylmethyl ketones attached to unusual sulfur-containing unsaturated rings and a cyclobutadiene-like small ring. Ring presence is 1.0 and aromatic presence 0.9345, with mean SMILES length 46.9; ring abundance coexists with substantial chemical strain.

Multiply bonded ring sulfur with additional substituents should not be read as ordinary thiophene or terminal thiocarbonyl chemistry.
Late cyclobutadiene-like rings are highly strained, and several related products also contain N-N or N-O bonds.
Thiol and chloromethyl decorations add reactivity concerns without a consistent local score advantage.
missing_features: Ordinary amide-nitrogen and ring alternatives retaining the leading carbonyl and aromatic arrangement are not established within the strongest strained-amide series.
Stable sulfur bonding and less strained fusion patterns are underrepresented around the late pyridyl ketones.
Chemically credible matched alternatives linking the conventional indole family to the higher-scoring unusual topology are absent.

method_name: Tabu search: de novo graph walks with expiring structural prohibitions
method_thesis: The anchor is the basic tabu-search procedure in Section 2 of [Glover, Tabu Search—Part I](https://leeds-faculty.colorado.edu/glover/TS%20-%20Part%20I-ORSA-aw.pdf), fixed before locating this external source. It chooses the best available admissible move, including a worsening move, while temporarily prohibiting reversals through short-term attribute memory. My molecular adaptation starts from the best supplied observation and maintains one current molecular graph, its true score, an independent best-observed archive, and expiring structural restrictions. At each feedback step, stochastically generate a new neighborhood through atom and bond edits, additions, deletions and chemically checked ring changes. Define move attributes from presence/absence changes of canonical local subgraphs around the edited region. After selecting a move, temporarily forbid a bounded record of its inverse attribute changes. These restrictions must apply to different canonical molecules sharing the affected local chemistry, so they can alter search beyond the protocol's mandatory whole-molecule duplicate rejection. Generate valid, canonical-unique, admissible neighbors until the announced batch is filled, then submit them directly without a learned score predictor. Only after real feedback choose the highest-scoring accepted neighbor as the next current graph, even when it scores below the current graph; retain the best score seen anywhere. Age restrictions by completed walk steps. If restrictions prevent sufficient fresh generation, release the oldest restrictions only as needed and record that release. This root uses the basic tabu form without an aspiration rule requiring unknown candidate scores. Preparation needs no learned model or corpus molecule store. Each objective restarts the same task-agnostic procedure with clean labeled and tabu state, and every proposed structure is generated online from the evolving current graph. The hypothesis is that an aggressive observed-neighbor choice combined with temporary structural reversal restrictions can move through useful intermediate structures and reach higher scoring molecular regions within the supplied feedback schedule. Activation requires restrictions to veto otherwise valid novel structural moves and thereby influence later current states. That diagnostic is insufficient by itself: success is the mean of the five independent final Top-1 scores. Overbroad attributes may suppress productive chemistry, while overly specific attributes may never affect novel proposals; the root must expose both possibilities.

molecular_assessment.headline: Sulfur-rich cages persist; a stronger aryl-amine family removes sulfur but retains strained nitrogen rings
molecular_assessment.overall_character: All supplied current and parent trajectories were inspected. Every objective has 900 entries, including 870 optimizer proposals, and none lacks trajectories. These are consistently substantial ring-containing molecules: ring-closure and branch presence rates are 1.0 throughout. Aromatic-token presence is also 1.0 on several populations, 0.9345 on the arylamide population, and 0.7184 on the sulfur-cage population. These are molecule-level text counters, not aromatic atom fractions, ring feasibility, or molecular conformations. The outputs range from recognizable indole carboxamides and aryl cyclic amines to heavily bridged N/O frameworks, long sulfur/oxygen side chains, and multiply bonded sulfur cages. Mean SMILES lengths range from 46.9 to 69.0; the main problem is not a population of trivial fragments or universally giant repeated assemblies. Rather, much of the visible variety changes decoration or connectivity within seed-specific complex families. Explicit charge and tetrahedral stereolabel rates are zero, despite potentially basic amines and stereogenic carbon or sulfur connectivity. Some current chemistry differs meaningfully from the parent, especially the sulfur-free aryl-amine leader, while other leading structures and entire chemical trajectories are unchanged. Apparent synthetic plausibility remains questionable and overall drug likeness weak because useful recognizable groups coexist with strained rings, unusual sulfur valence, reactive heteroatom-halogen bonds, and undefined stereochemistry.
